text:
This guidance for importing line managers explains the process for transferring employees across the Civil Service.

Guidance for employees transferring across the Civil Service and exporting managers provide an overview of the whole process.

Departments using the new digital Employee Transfer Service

The employee’s provisional job offer email will tell them if their transfer uses the digital service.

If an employee’s transfer is between 2 departments who use the digital service, their transfer will:

follow separate guidance contained in the service

not use the Excel-based staff transfer form

If you need to progress a transfer between departments who use the Employee Transfer Service, you will receive an email explaining how to access the service.

If your department does not use the digital service, use the Excel-based staff transfer form on GOV.UK.

If the wrong form is used, this will delay the employee’s transfer.

About staff transfers

A lot of employees move across the Civil Service. The staff transfer process helps employees move between government departments without resigning.

The staff transfer process contains separate actions for:

transferring employees

their current line manager

their current HR/Shared services

you, as their new line manager

The staff transfer form helps employees progress through their transfer. It collects and shares the information needed for a move between government departments.

Who the staff transfer process applies to

It applies to civil servants who are transferring permanently or on a loan of 6 months or more between:

ministerial and non-ministerial departments and their executive agencies

the following crown non-departmental public bodies (NDPB) employing civil servants:

Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service (ACAS)

Health and Safety Executive (HSE)

Institute for Apprenticeships and Technical Education (IfATE)

Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR)

If the employee is employed by any other NDPB or are a public servant - they can apply for some roles within the Civil Service, but this transfer process would not apply to them.

Departments, agencies and public bodies lists departments, non-departmental public bodies and other bodies.

The staff transfer process also applies to civil servants transferring from the Scottish and Welsh governments and the Northern Ireland Civil Service (NICS).

To be eligible, the employee’s original appointment must be on merit and by fair and open competition.

Exceptions

The staff transfer form is mandatory except for:

machinery of government changes. For example, these involve whole business areas transferring between departments

Cabinet Office statement of practice (COSOP) moves

if the employee is a civil servant on a loan of less than 6 months

How employees transfer

They will get an email confirming their provisional job offer from the relevant recruitment team.

They will need to complete Parts A-1 and A-2 of the staff transfer form. This is otherwise known as the Civil Service Employee Transfer (CSET) form. It covers HR, payroll and security clearance transfer. Their current line manager and HR/shared services also have sections of the form to complete.

The staff transfer process puts the employee at the centre of the process. They are responsible for starting the transfer. The employee provides most of the information needed to progress their transfer. This includes personal details and information about both their current and new role. The employee does not resign when they transfer between departments.

There are actions for importing line managers/vacancy holders transferring an employee into their department. You should make sure the employee joins your department’s payroll by providing:

salary

start date

security confirmation

You need to complete the New Entrant Notification (NEN) form or your department’s equivalent as quickly as possible.

If you need help with the staff transfer process

If you need help, contact your:

recruitment provider (if applicable) or HR team/Shared Services

HR Business Partner

vacancy holder (if different from yourself)

vetting or security cluster
